findings.title: U2 and U4 form a circular implementation dependency
findings.section: U2 - Generalize the atomic replacement transaction / U4 - Add authenticated interaction holds
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers cannot follow the declared unit order: U2 says U4 supplies the hold guard before end-to-end enablement, while U4 declares the U2 transaction seam as a prerequisite. That leaves it unclear which U2 work is expected to land before U4 and which work is deferred, risking partial-unit rework or enabling replacement without the required hold guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the U2 dependency into an explicitly named transaction seam that lands before U4 and a post-U4 completion step, then make U4 depend on that seam and make the remaining U2 work depend on U4.
evidence: U2. Generalize the atomic replacement transaction — Dependencies: U1 observation identity contract; U4 supplies the hold guard before end-to-end enablement.
U4. Add authenticated interaction holds and transport lifetime — Dependencies: U2 transaction seam.

resolved_findings.reason: The integration fence already prevents early publication, but listing U4 under U2 Dependencies can be read as a graph cycle. Separate the build dependency from the existing integration fence; no split or product change is needed.
resolved_findings.change: U2 depends on U1 and produces a transaction/guard seam. U4 connects the hold guard; publication remains disabled until U3–U5 integrate.
resolved_findings.verification: U1 -> U2 -> U3/U4 -> U5 -> U6 -> U7 -> U8 is acyclic; existing publication fence and Product Contract unchanged.
